title: Nonblocking and poll semantics avoid ambiguous retries
summary: The library wraps poll readiness in semantic watch/result objects and treats nonblocking behavior deliberately. sendAll refuses nonblocking descriptors because a partial prefix followed by EAGAIN cannot be blindly retried without duplication risk.
invariants: UnixPoll exposes readable/writable/priority/error/hangup/invalid semantics rather than requiring application code to decode raw poll bitmasks.
sendAll is a blocking-only convenience and must refuse a nonblocking descriptor.
A poll watch resolves the target descriptor at wait time; it must not intentionally retain a stale fd after target close/release.
procedure: For nonblocking protocols, drive send/receive progress from semantic readiness and track application-level partial progress explicitly.

provenance.claim: UnixPollWatch/UnixPoll/UnixPollResult implement semantic poll readiness over profile-defined poll bits.
Nonblocking mode, wouldBlock and sendAll blocking-only refusal are implemented in the class.
